milestone.title: raul Milestones table refactor — table visual with indent + lifecycle gauge, multi-select lifecycle filter, drop Grooming tab

intent.outcome: The Milestones tab uses the same Table widget as Backlog (proper row cursor via highlight_style(REVERSED)), adds a lifecycle gauge column showing position in the canonical lifecycle path, and a multi-select lifecycle filter modal so users can show any combination (approved, in-progress, remediation, done, ...). The old Grooming tab is gone — its semantics (approved + in-progress + groomed) are reachable via the Grooming preset bound to g.

problem.description: Today's Milestones tab uses a custom line-span renderer with only BOLD applied to id-substring spans as the selected-row signal — no row-wide cursor, weak highlight. Backlog uses a Table widget with highlight_style(REVERSED), proper row cursor. The asymmetry makes navigation feel different on the two list-surfacing tabs. The Grooming tab is one hard-coded filter (approved + in-progress + groomed); users who want remediation-only or done-only have no way to express that. There is no visual indicator of lifecycle position — a colored badge is the only signal. The lifecycle rank table in app.rs (in-progress > approved > groomed > done > self-reviewed > reviewed > complete > cancelled > remediation > draft) is the canonical ordering and is the right shape for a gauge.

in_scope: Drop Lane::Grooming from Lane::ordered() and from the dispatcher in app.rs render() match

Replace render_milestone_tree in lane_lists.rs:419 with a Table-widget-based renderer matching Backlog's visual (highlight_style(REVERSED), column layout with id, title, priority, lifecycle gauge, lifecycle)
Add an indent column showing depends_on[0] depth (small left indent, max ~4 spaces)

Add a lifecycle gauge column: 8 segments (draft → groomed → approved → in-progress → done → self-reviewed → reviewed → complete); the segment for the current lifecycle is filled and palette-colored, segments before are dim filled, segments after are empty; cancelled shows ✗, remediation shows ↺ instead of the segmented bar
Extend crates/raul/src/tui/progress.rs (not a new module) with the lifecycle gauge widget
Add app.milestone_filter: BTreeSet<Lifecycle> state on App (empty = all)
New mode: Mode::LifecycleFilter — multi-select modal with Space toggle, arrows navigate, Enter commit, Esc revert
New actions: OpenLifecycleFilter, LifecycleFilterToggle, LifecycleFilterNext/Prev, LifecycleFilterCommit, LifecycleFilterCancel, ApplyGroomingPreset
Title bar chip on Milestones: 'Milestones · approved, in-progress (8)' when filter is non-empty, 'Milestones · All (12)' when empty
g keybind applies the Grooming preset (approved + in-progress + groomed)
Filter state persists across lane switches (same lifetime as hide_done and lane_sort_key)
Pin parity tests: synthetic milestone set → expected rendered order; synthetic lifecycle set → expected gauge segment for each lifecycle
out_of_scope: Filter modal for Backlog/Ideas (a separate title-bar filter chip is a follow-up; M185's modal is Milestones-only)
Backlog table refactor (M184 already keeps the existing Backlog renderer; M185 lifts the shared helper but does not change Backlog visually)
True fuzzy matching on the lifecycle filter (the filter is a multi-select set, not a search)
Changing the underlying MilestoneSummary shape in mp (priority, updated, depends_on already carry enough)
Any new keybinds beyond F (filter), g (preset), and the modal-internal keys
Refactoring the existing render_milestone_tree module (crates/raul/src/tui/render/milestone_tree.rs); it can stay as-is — only the lane_lists.rs:419 caller is replaced

design_decisions.choice: Lifecycle gauge as a column between priority and lifecycle-at on the Milestones table
design_decisions.rationale: Right-anchored so titles (left-anchored) keep maximum width; the gauge width is fixed (8 cells + padding) regardless of terminal width — the existing list_title_col_width helper in lane_lists.rs already handles column-flex behavior.

design_decisions.choice: 8 segments in the order draft → groomed → approved → in-progress → done → self-reviewed → reviewed → complete; cancelled and remediation render as off-path markers (✗ and ↺)
design_decisions.rationale: This matches the canonical lifecycle path the mp toolkit treats as forward-flowing. Off-path states (cancelled, remediation) are not part of the linear progression and need a distinct marker so the gauge doesn't lie about position.

design_decisions.choice: g keybind applies the preset; no separate Grooming tab; the preset is encoded as a constant filter set
design_decisions.rationale: Preserves old Grooming tab muscle memory for users who relied on it. Encoding the preset as a constant filter set (rather than a separate rendering mode) keeps the rendering path simple and means the chip + the preset are the same code path.

design_decisions.choice: Persist app.milestone_filter alongside hide_done and lane_sort_key (in-memory across lane switches; cleared on raul restart for this milestone — MP_HOME persistence is a follow-up if users want it)
design_decisions.rationale: Same persistence model as existing in-memory user preferences. MP_HOME persistence can be added later if it becomes a UX gap.

design_decisions.choice: Indent column shows depends_on[0] depth (1 space per level, capped at ~4 spaces) as a leading column
design_decisions.rationale: Preserves the 'tree feel' of the previous render_milestone_tree without committing to full tree glyphs — at scale (50+ milestones), pure tree glyphs get noisy. Indent is the minimum cue needed to see hierarchy; deeper relationships are surfaced via the title text.

Update the 7 production files that reference Lane::Grooming: (1) crates/raul/src/tui/app.rs — drop the enum variant, Lane::Grooming arm in Lane::ordered(), compact_label match, sort_keys_for match (collapse to Milestones + Ideas + Backlog only), visible_backlog list-size dispatch (line 969), and the Grooming special-case branch in visible_milestones (the legacy 'approved || in-progress || groomed' filter is replaced by the new milestone_filter mechanism in WP2); (2) crates/raul/src/tui/runner_helpers.rs — remove Lane::Grooming from valid_lanes in load_persisted_sort_keys, from match_lane_label, and from the data-loader dispatch (Lane::Grooming currently calls load_milestones — collapse to Milestones only); (3) crates/raul/src/tui/render/lane_lists.rs — drop the Grooming arm in render_lane_list; (4) crates/raul/src/tui/view_state.rs — drop Lane::Grooming from the scrollbar-rect dispatch match (line 598); (5) crates/raul/src/tui/action.rs — remove the Lane::Grooming arm in the Enter-key handler (it called enter_milestone_detail; that path is now reachable via Milestones); (6) crates/raul/src/lanes.rs — drop LANE_GROOMING references in the lane_label match; (7) crates/raul/src/path_tree_model.rs — line 80 maps the 'grooming' lane string for the Path tab's lifecycle branches; verify whether the path data still emits this branch and update if needed. Also: remove the body string 'Grooming requested via raul TUI' in crates/raul/src/tui/runner_helpers.rs:471 if its caller is removed; trace the consumer before removal.
steps.done_when: Lane::Grooming is no longer referenced anywhere; Lane::ordered() returns 7 lanes; App::visible_milestones() no longer has the Grooming special case. A test pins Lane::ordered() shape.

steps.action: Replace render_milestone_tree (lane_lists.rs:419) with a Table-widget-based renderer matching Backlog's visual. Columns: indent (depends_on[0] depth, 1 space per level capped at 4), id, title (fill), priority, lifecycle gauge, lifecycle-at. Use highlight_style(REVERSED) for the selected row. As part of this step, delete the entire crates/raul/src/tui/render/milestone_tree.rs module (the file becomes dead code after the Table renderer lands): drop the pub mod milestone_tree; declaration in render/mod.rs:18, drop the use crate::tui::render::milestone_tree; in render/lane_lists.rs:10, and remove the file itself. The lifecycle_color helper inside milestone_tree.rs is moved to progress.rs in step S3 — do not lose it during deletion.
steps.done_when: Milestones tab renders via a Table widget with REVERSED cursor; a test asserts the cursor lands on the correct row (REVERSED style applied to that row only).

steps.action: Extend crates/raul/src/tui/progress.rs (not a new module) with lifecycle_gauge_segment(lifecycle: &str) → &str helper and lifecycle_color(lifecycle: &str, palette: &Palette) → Color (moved from milestone_tree.rs which is deleted in step S2 — preserve the exact mapping: complete → success, in-progress → accent, blocked → danger, approved / ready → warn, else → dim). 8 canonical lifecycles map to a segmented bar position: draft=0, groomed=1, approved=2, in-progress=3, done=4, self-reviewed=5, reviewed=6, complete=7. Cancelled shows ✗ (using palette.danger), remediation shows ↺ (using palette.warn). Add a render function that draws the gauge as 8 cells (▮ for the current segment + filled palette color, ▮ dim for prior segments, ▯ for future segments). Wire it into the Milestones table column between priority and lifecycle-at. A test pins each lifecycle → (segment_index, color) pair.
steps.done_when: Each lifecycle renders the correct segment; the gauge is visible in the Milestones table; a test pins each lifecycle → segment mapping.

Filter state is in-memory and survives lane switches (same lifetime as hide_done).

steps.action: Add Mode::LifecycleFilter variant. Add actions: OpenLifecycleFilter, LifecycleFilterToggle, LifecycleFilterNext, LifecycleFilterPrev, LifecycleFilterCommit, LifecycleFilterCancel. The modal UI: list of 10 lifecycles (draft, groomed, approved, in-progress, done, self-reviewed, reviewed, complete, cancelled, remediation) in canonical order with cancelled and remediation at the bottom as off-path branches; arrows navigate; Space toggles a lifecycle (added/removed from app.milestone_filter); Enter commits; Esc reverts to the prior filter state. Modal size: if content_area.height < 17 rows, the lifecycle list becomes scrollable (only the visible window renders) and a 'more below' indicator appears — never overflows the content area. Implement the modal renderer in render/overlays.rs (parallel to the Settings flat-list pattern). On mode close, the placeholder per-tab footer label added in the M183 footer milestone is replaced by the real modal-internal keys. Keybind coexistence: lowercase f continues to bind Action::ToggleFilter (annotation open-only toggle in the annotation thread view) — both f and F coexist; the help overlay text added in the help-overlay-sync step below explicitly notes the case distinction.

steps.action: Add ApplyGroomingPreset action. Bind g to it. The action sets app.milestone_filter to {Lifecycle::Approved, Lifecycle::InProgress, Lifecycle::Groomed} (the legacy Grooming tab semantics). Lane-gating: the action is a no-op on lanes other than Milestones — pressing g on Path/Overview/Watch/Settings/Backlog/Ideas does nothing. Title bar chip and visible_milestones() reflect the new filter immediately when applied. A test pins the preset's filter set; a second test pins the no-op behavior on each non-Milestone lane.
steps.done_when: Pressing g applies the Grooming preset; app.milestone_filter has the three expected lifecycles; title bar shows them. A test pins the preset's filter set.

steps.action: Render the title bar chip on Milestones: 'Milestones · <comma-separated-filter> (<count>)' when app.milestone_filter is non-empty, 'Milestones · All (<count>)' when empty. The count is the post-filter count from visible_milestones() (also honoring hide_done). Chip design: one segment for the lifecycle filter only in this milestone; M186 will add a second segment for the search term separated by ' · '. The chip uses the dim palette color so it doesn't compete with the lane title; the active segment is rendered with the palette accent color. Touch render/dashboard_view.rs and/or render/mod.rs to render the chip.
steps.done_when: Title bar shows the chip with the correct text in both states; a test pins both states against a fixture set.
